findings.text: §4's done-when has four cases (insert refused, insert-in-`<code>` accepted, text edit adding nothing accepted, audit-doc warns), and neither a create-path refusal nor a text-mode refusal is among them, so the two paths the section adds are never shown to refuse; the text-mode channel in particular converts the predicate's `OpError` into `ValueError`, and a case that only requires an *accept* passes whether that conversion is implemented or not

findings.reason: the section's scope, its write-path list and its test plan are set for two new call sites where one is needed, and a worker told to wire the predicate onto the create path would be looking for an entry point that does not exist outside the section funnel.
findings.text: §4 says "Plan creation through `edit_plan`'s create and the text-mode write do not reach it", but `append sections` carrying a body is the create route (reckon/_store.py:3062-3065) and queues the body through `_queue_authored_section` (:3371) as a `section_insertions` effect, which the write path applies by calling `_insert_authored_section` (:1418-1419) and so already runs `_refuse_forged_body_structure` (:946) over it; only the text-mode path is genuinely new

findings.reason: the enumeration in the same sentence is complete and correct, so the mechanism (extend the shared predicate rather than write a second check) is unaffected.
